 Punahou Students and Faculty Gather for Election Day Watch Party
 Academy Campus News Civics Faculty and Staff · November 6, 2026 · 2 min read 
 Punahou’s Davis Democracy Fellows hosted an Election Day Watch Party on Tuesday, Nov. 3, bringing students, faculty and staff together in Luke Lecture Hall to follow election returns and explore issues shaping the political landscape. Entire classes also attended throughout the day, including Senior English Honors, two sections of ninth-grade English 1 and two sections of sixth-grade social studies.
 Organized through the Davis Democracy Initiative, the event featured presentations from students, educators, alumni and guest speakers on topics ranging from U.S. foreign policy and campaign financing to climate change, media influence and the role of faith in politics.
 The day’s speakers and presentations included:
 Dr. Stephen Noerper: Impact on U.S. Foreign Policy                 
 Christian Kaakua ’28, Brooke Watari ’29 and Riley Joe ’28: Kids Voting Hawaiʻi, a nonpartisan civic education program that introduces K – 12 students to the voting process through mock elections.
 Zane Dalgamouni ’29: The Youth Vote, highlighting the growing influence of young voters and ways students can become more involved in the political process.
 Dr. Bonnie Christensen: Campaign Financing
 Dr. Debbie Millikan: Sustainability & Climate Change
 Sara Markowitz ’28: Contemporary Media in Politics, presenting on behalf of Olesya Noerper ’28.
 Chaplain Luana Uluave: Faith in Politics
 Robert Gelber ’92, Punahou Communications Director: How Politicians Use Rhetorical Reframing to Counter Negative Narratives
 Amelia Sofos ’24: Party Politics
 Dr. Michael Latham ’86, Punahou President: History of Elections and U.S. Foreign Policy, including Iran and Ukraine   
 The event also featured a presentation of political posters by Academy students in the Arts & Letters course, taught by Alison Lazzara ’93 and Josh Tollefson.
 The daylong gathering encouraged civic engagement, thoughtful discussion and a deeper understanding of the democratic process as participants followed election developments together.
